source.authoredBasis: Four authored graph windows from the complete equations: A solid 2^x vs dashed x+1; B solid .3^x vs dashed x+1; C and D solid 2^x vs dashed x^2-2, respectively negative and positive windows. Both sides are rendered, including the positive near-miss; no root markers, values or answer-bearing labels are added. These are new analytic plots, not invented original scans.

notes: All A-D panels visible. A: increasing exponential and increasing straight line, distinguishable dashed/solid strokes. B: decreasing exponential and increasing straight line. C: negative window of exponential/parabola with fine 0.1 x grid and one visible crossing; D: positive window x=2..4 shows separate near-miss curves, with no intersection marker. Final y=18/x=4 and bottom labels are present. All eight full path sequences match the respective formulas in their own labeled frames. Quantitative windows are A=(-2..3,-1..8), B=(-1..2,-1..4), C=(-2..0,-2..4), D=(2..4,2..18). D's lower border is y=2, not y=0; tick labels honestly state that offset. A finite viewport is not proof of global root completeness; that belongs to the source solve and question check. Full image actually viewed once; visible labels are English/numerical, no cultural marks, solutions or correct-option annotations. Neutral semantic SVG colors and clear strokes. Scratch-path packaging is pending the parent, not a second mathematical gate.
